notes_for_pm: Android has two unpair entry points with materially different effects (Settings clears credentials only, leaving a live session, a running foreground service and a stale OS bond). FR-17 reconciles them into one canonical unpair. This is a deliberate divergence from Android behaviour and should be recorded in the Parity Ledger as a fix, not a loss.

The advertise-and-wait Driver's force-first-pair switch exists on Android but is unreachable from the pairing UI, so every Medtronic re-pair advertises FIRST_PAIR. FR-6 exposes it from the Re-pair entry point. Also a fix rather than a port.

Tandem Pumps accept exactly one BLE connection at a time. This collides with Tandem's own iOS app, with any macOS validation bench, and with any Watch-side experiment. FR-7's 'another app or device is connected to your pump' message is the only diagnostic that distinguishes it from a broken pairing, and it will be a recurring support case for Builders who keep t:connect installed.

All vendor-specific pairing copy moves into the Driver (FR-2), with a CI-checkable assertion that the shared pairing views contain no vendor strings. Android hard-coded Tandem copy into the central-scan branch, which mislabels any contributed Driver (relevant to UJ-6).

FR-15 depends on a Settings surface (background-monitoring health) whose information architecture belongs to 5.9; FR-15 and FR-16 depend on notification delivery that belongs to 5.4. Both cross-references are called out inline so the sections can be reconciled.

plugins/example is NOT listed in Android's settings.gradle.kts - verified directly. It is a standalone JVM project producing a sideloadable JAR, not a built module of the app. FR-35 (Simulated Driver) and FR-36 (Trace-Replay Driver) are therefore net-new engineering, not a port, and they sit on the critical path: with no Core Bluetooth in the iOS Simulator and no iPhone for the lead developer, they are the only executable Drivers during most development.

The Android source carries a three-way Driver API version drift: code says PLUGIN_API_VERSION = 5, docs/dev/plugin-architecture.md says 2, and plugins/example's META-INF/plugin.json and README say 1 - meaning Android's own shipped example JAR would be rejected by its own loader today. The Android docs also omit the bolus-category provider Capability entirely and reference SafetyLimits property names (glucoseLow/glucoseHigh/maxBolus) that do not exist. Port from the Kotlin source, never from the Android documentation.

Android's four deprecated pump interfaces (PumpDriver, PumpConnectionManager, PumpScanner, HistoryLogParser) and their four registry adapters are deliberately NOT ported. Two carry live defects: HistoryLogParserAdapter returns an empty list when no Driver is active (indistinguishable from 'the patient had no boluses'), and the deprecated signatures default their SafetyLimits parameter to the absolute bounds whenever a caller omits the user's narrowed configuration. FR-33 and FR-32 exist to make both impossible.

FR-31 requires a Required Check that fails the build if a Driver target imports anything beyond the shared safety module, the Driver API and Core Bluetooth. This is the compile-time replacement for Android's RestrictedContext sandbox and needs a concrete gate definition in 5.11.

Section 5.2 assumes 5.11 owns the CI gate definitions for: Driver Catalog completeness (unregistered Driver fails), Driver ID / settings-key regex enforcement, Driver API version assertion, the therapy-write denylist, and the Driver-target import lint. All five are referenced here as Required Checks but not defined here.

Parity loss - guaranteed refresh cadence: Android's foreground service polled every 15 s and doubled as the ~30 s BLE keep-alive. iOS has no periodic background execution, so the dashboard cannot guarantee current data while backgrounded. FR-41 (foreground re-read) plus FR-48/49/50 (honest degradation) are the substitute.
Parity loss - chart detail orientation: no 'sensor landscape' on iOS, no per-screen orientation property, geometry request not honoured on iPad, and a different rotation-lock interaction.

Parity loss - Bluetooth glyph: no system Bluetooth SF Symbol, and the Bluetooth SIG marks are trademark-encumbered. A custom six-state glyph set must ship; if the marks cannot be used the status-row vocabulary diverges from the published Android status-icons doc.

Deliberate divergence - numeric formatting: FR-60 requires dot-decimal and half-up rounding for EVERY dashboard number. Android forces US formatting only inside its glucose formatter and uses device locale elsewhere (mixed separators on a comma-decimal device), and Java %f is half-up while Foundation String(format:) is half-to-even (12.5% -> '12%', mean 100.5 -> '100' in a naive port). Intentional improvement; record in the Parity Ledger as an intentional divergence.

Preserved inconsistency: severity banding treats a value exactly at 'low'/'high' as Low/High while the Time in Range aggregate counts both as in-range. Both pinned by test; recommendation is to preserve and record rather than silently reconcile.

Light-theme contrast: Green #22C55E and Yellow #EAB308 fail WCAG AA for small text on white (TIR legend, CGM-stats subtitles, age caption). Hues are a cross-surface semantic contract - darken only the text variants in the Light appearance.

Glyph coverage risk: U+21C8 / U+21CA may not be covered by the system font at 40pt bold, on the most-read element in the app. Ship a custom glyph pair if the fallback is visible, keeping the Unicode string as the data contract so app and Watch app stay string-identical.

App Review sensitivity: shipping Tandem / Medtronic / Nightscout brand marks is inherited nominative use; Apple reviews third-party trademarks less predictably than Google Play. All marks stay behind one asset lookup so the set can be disabled with a single change.

Two behaviours were deliberately hardened relative to Android under SI-2: TimeInRangeData's invariant check and FreshnessThresholds' ordering check must be failable/throwing and render the empty state, never a precondition that would trap a monitoring app mid-background-wake.

Nine Parity Ledger entries enumerated at the end of the section (DND/silent-switch override, alarm volume boost, vibration waveforms, permanently visible watching indicator, Backend delivery to a suspended app, launch on boot, background evaluation cadence, wrist notification sounds, plus one parity GAIN on wrist-silencing a floor alarm).

Open question: does the Coverage Claim state say 'watching' or 'watching, but you may not hear it' when Critical Alerts is absent? FR-66 currently puts the caveat in claim detail copy, not claim state. Needs a product ruling — it would appear for nearly every Builder nearly all the time.
Open question: FR-76's re-alarm ladder (5 repeats at 120 s) is invented, not ported. It substitutes for two Android mechanisms with no iOS analog and needs a real-user tuning pass before first tag.

Open question: FR-86's background evaluation cadence cannot be measured without an iPhone plus Pump. Lead developer has neither (decision 10), so it lands on DanielDanielson's fork build against their t:slim X2 (decision 9). Sequence early — the honest response to a slow cadence is a coverage-copy change, not a wider Fresh boundary.

Cross-section dependency: 5.9 owns notification authorization request and settings UI, but FR-66 and FR-83 consume UNNotificationSettings (criticalAlertSetting, timeSensitiveSetting, scheduledDeliverySetting) as Coverage Claim inputs. 5.9 must ensure the request includes .criticalAlert and .providesAppNotificationSettings and NEVER .provisional.

Cross-section dependency: 5.7 owns Watch rendering, the widget timelines and the Live Activity, but FR-84 fixes the contract they must honor — one validUntil number drives the widget timeline entry, the Live Activity staleDate, the Watch decay, and the FR-85 lapse notification. Forking the claim pipeline per surface is prohibited.

Cross-section dependency: 5.8 owns SSE transport and the APNs deferral rationale; FR-71's degraded predicate consumes the stream state and FR-85 states the product consequence (Backend alerts do not reach a suspended or terminated app in v1).

Parity Ledger entries owned by 5.5: the draggable meal entry button is dropped for a fixed entry point plus a Home list row; iOS has no catchable out-of-memory condition so the 'photo too large to process' state is reached by prevention plus a launch-time recovery marker; after a camera-permission denial iOS never re-prompts, so the app can only deep-link to Settings.

One deliberate improvement over Android also belongs in the Parity Ledger: the Recent Boluses / Bolus History BG column renders in the user's display unit with a label, where Android prints the raw mg/dL integer. Confirm this divergence is wanted before it is pinned by tests.

SI-12 carve-out requested for the dispersion flags (wideSpread defaults false, identityAgreement defaults true) so a missing field never fabricates a caution. Needs an explicit ruling because it conflicts with SI-12 unless the Contract Pin marks them optional.

FR-89 through FR-92 are journey-orphaned: UJ-5 covers meals only and there is no journey for reviewing delivered insulin. Consider adding one so FR-90's requested-vs-delivered honesty rule has a narrative anchor.

The Android 5xx meal diagnostic log (200-char body excerpt) is carried forward only under SI-9 scrubbing; if the scrubber cannot guarantee a Backend error body carries no food identity or carb value, the log must be dropped rather than weakened.
Open question: does the Backend ever return an image URL for a food record? Android renders a neutral placeholder thumbnail because it does not; iOS inherits that assumption.

Open question: the Simulator has no camera, so the entire meal capture entry point is device-only. A debug bundled-sample-photo injector is specified in FR-94 to keep the preparation and upload path exercisable — confirm it is in v1 scope.

S2 defines no user journey for AI Chat. UJ-1 through UJ-6 cover glanceability, overnight lows, building, pairing, meals and contribution - none touches chat. The section is written journey-less rather than forcing a reference; either that stands or S2 gains a seventh journey.

Android's onboarding copy already promises daily briefs while the client ships no brief surface and never calls the brief endpoints. That inconsistency ports along with the copy unless 5.9 fixes the onboarding wording.

Defect fixed rather than ported: Android's Watch chat watchdog (30 s) is shorter than its phone-side AI call (90 s), so a slow-but-successful answer can surface as a wrist timeout while the phone completes and pushes a response that replaces the error. FR-114 mandates one shared timeout across both surfaces, closing the window.

The AI-provider probe deliberately uses the short general Backend timeout while the chat call uses the long AI request timeout - a slow inference must not count toward any Backend-health signal. 5.8 owns the general timeout value; 5.6 owns the AI one.
Whether the Watch app calls the Backend directly or relays through the app is left to 5.8. This section fixes only the behaviour contract, which must hold identically under either transport.

Two Android defects are fixed during the port rather than carried over: (a) the alert dismiss now carries the alert identifier instead of an empty payload (Android can dismiss the wrong alert when two arrive in quick succession, documented at wear-os-architecture.md:112), and (b) both graph surfaces get Freshness Tier de-emphasis plus a single unified Y clamp (Android ships 20/500 on the sparkline and 40/400 on the detail view, so a reading below 40 is visible on one surface and clipped off the other, and neither surface de-emphasises stale data at all).

Open question owed to S15: should the Watch app get an independent data path to the Backend in Backend-connected mode (its own background fetch)? It is the honest answer to 'the phone died', but it puts a Backend credential in the Watch Keychain and creates a second data path with its own freshness semantics. 5.8 owns the Backend contract; 5.7 only needs to know whether the wrist ever sources data from anywhere but the app.

Three FR-level behaviours are only provable on hardware and must be budgeted as device time from project start, not discovered late: felt haptic per alert tier, wrist breakthrough with Sleep Focus on, and complications still updating after 18 hours of continuous use (the metered refresh allowance is not enforced in the Simulator, so a push-per-reading design appears to work in development and silently stops mid-day on device).

The greyscale distinguishability gate in the feature NFRs is written as merge-blocking. If PM wants it advisory instead, the coverage-honesty encoding in FR-126 loses its only enforcement and the Android dead-phone cue is silently deleted on iOS.

FR-125 deliberately splits threshold fallback defaults (70/180/55/250) into display-banding-only use, so SI-5 is not violated: no wrist alert is ever scheduled from a default threshold. Android does not draw this distinction explicitly and the port should not inherit the ambiguity.

Two Android constants are deliberately changed for iOS and need sign-off: the outbound queue bound (5,000 -> 20,000 rows, FR-142) and the stale-in-flight reclaim window (60s -> 15 min, FR-141). Both exist because iOS defers work Android performed immediately; Android's values would discard pump history during a normal overnight suspension.

Four Android defects are closed rather than reproduced: raw pump-history cleanup that had zero production callers (FR-139); alert retention that only ran when the alerts screen was opened (FR-139); post-login fetches running on the sign-in screen's scope (FR-156); a server URL's path prefix being silently dropped (FR-150).

FR-155 carries the single largest new-defect risk in the section: Swift's synthesized Codable does not apply property defaults for absent keys, so fields Moshi tolerated (is_automated, acknowledged, raw_accepted, raw_duplicates, source) become hard parse failures unless every one is decoded with an explicit default. The contract smoke test must assert every defaulted field decodes when absent - an assertion Android cannot even fail.

FR-135/FR-136/FR-151 depend on behavior the iOS Simulator does not enforce (file protection, Keychain lock-state accessibility, Local Network privacy). The section states that a Simulator result for these is treated as NO result; given the lead developer has no iPhone, this makes maintainer DanielDanielson's device the only validation path for those requirements.

FR-157 keeps the device-token field in the registration payload unpopulated so adopting APNs later needs no contract change. If the PM wants the field removed instead, that is a Contract Pin question for 5.11.

Parity Ledger entries owned by 5.9, enumerated in the section Notes: no system sound picker; no notification channels; no system-volume boost; no watch-face gallery/push/face-level options; no in-app self-update or watch-app push; no runtime Driver install; no battery-optimization exemption; ATS cannot be scoped to private address ranges; Local Network Privacy is a new failure mode with no Android counterpart.

Research contradiction flagged: it recommends 'a scoped ATS exception via NSExceptionDomains' in one place while stating elsewhere that exception domains accept neither IPs nor CIDR, and that NSAllowsLocalNetworking causes NSAllowsArbitraryLoads to be ignored. Only one shape works — blanket cleartext at the platform layer with NO local-networking key, app policy as sole guard. Section is written to that shape; needs a one-line confirmation in the architecture addendum.
The glucose-unit seed notice copy names Nightscout on Android. Under decision 8 the app is not a Nightscout client, so FR-175 reads 'Nightscout-sourced data'. Confirm wording.
FR-177's accessibility-identifier registry and its Required Check are specified in 5.9 but enforced by CI in 5.11; the two need exactly one owner.

Every acceptance criterion in this section depending on lock state, Focus, ring/silent switch, Local Network Privacy, or Keychain/file-protection classes is device-only — the Simulator passes them while a real phone fails. These land on DanielDanielson's fork-built validation pass (decision 9).

Side-by-side stable + development install on one iPhone: free on Android via applicationIdSuffix, but on iOS costs every Builder a second globally-unique App ID, provisioning profile, App Store Connect record and TestFlight setup — roughly doubling onboarding. FR-183 assumes one identifier with a branch-selectable channel. Must be decided before the FR-182 provisioning workflow is built, because it changes what that workflow registers.

Build number derivation (FR-191) is a decision, not a port: clock-derived monotonic value plus a never-decreasing BUILD_NUMBER_OFFSET repository variable. Android's packed versionCode formula (major*1_000_000 + minor*10_000 + patch) is deliberately abandoned because it collides silently at patch > 9999 or minor > 99. The offset escape hatch should be exercised once before the first release.

Upstream may still want a 1Password-backed local convenience path for the lead's own maintainer builds. It must never become a project-held signing identity and must not be referenced from any fork-facing workflow — flagging so it is a deliberate choice rather than a leftover.

The legal framing of a Builder as builder, signer and installer-to-self (whether 'users become the manufacturer of their own personal medical device' now describes every user rather than only fork users) affects the wording of the build-and-install documentation. That determination belongs to 5.12 and to counsel; 5.10 states the builder relationship factually and asserts no legal conclusion.

The Android promotion pipeline is documented as 'built, unit-proven in parts, never exercised end to end' and its lockfile-regeneration path as an 'UNPROVEN PATH'. Recorded as a feature-specific NFR: exercise the full promotion/changelog/sync-back cycle on a throwaway repository before the first iOS release.

The auto-merge label relay (auto-merge-renovate.yml) must be AUTHORED here, not ported: Android's docs and workflow-security allowlist name a file that does not exist in that repository. Either write it or remove every reference including its allowlist entry.

CodeRabbit's Android config sets fail_commit_status: false, making even its mode: error custom checks (Medical Safety Review, BLE Protocol Safety) advisory with respect to merge blocking. This section moves those invariants into the type system, the Driver API-surface snapshot and replay tests so review is defence in depth; whether to also flip the commit status to failing is a deliberate decision, not a default to inherit.

UI Tests (Simulator) is non-required while it stabilizes, matching Android's emulator lane. Android has carried that 'while it beds in' state indefinitely with no promotion criterion. A stated trigger (e.g. N consecutive green runs) would prevent the same drift here.

The dependency license allowlist gate has no Android analogue in the evidence. Its initial contents must be set from the resolved graph at implementation time, and the GPL-3.0-only vs MIT/Apache-2.0 interaction (notably the EC-JPAKE implementation) is a licensing judgment belonging to 5.12's owner.

Cost pressure: required gates move to macOS runners (~10x billing multiplier on private repos). Keeping the upstream repository public and splitting platform-independent modules onto swift test is what keeps the required-check set affordable; a private upstream would create pressure to weaken it.

The Android contributor documentation carries at least six drifts from actual CI behavior (CONTRIBUTING lists five checks and calls Workflow Lint advisory zizmor when it is a hard-failing actionlint gate; claims the SAST gate scans the diff when it scans whole directory roots; two local-repro snippets scan less than CI; one gate has no documented repro; a workflow header claims to be the only workflow among eighteen). FR-197 and FR-213 close this structurally rather than by copying prose - do not let the prose be ported.

Android defects closed rather than reproduced: no CI validation of frontmatter or pages-array membership (a new page silently failed to publish); no link checker anywhere; a PR template CONTRIBUTING tells contributors to fill out but which does not exist; the dangling docs/dev/monorepo-port-ledger.md reference; six inconsistent repository slugs across policy documents; and the EC-JPAKE file carrying a prose port note but no Apache-2.0 identifier and no Particle Industries copyright, which Apache-2.0 requires travel with the file.

The highest-severity risk in this section is not technical: a naive swap to an off-the-shelf Swift license tool (LicensePlist et al.) converts five build-breaking guarantees into zero warnings, and nobody notices until a user reads a blank license screen. The generator must be written in-repo and fail-closed, and the drift test must exist on day one.

The install runbook is the only product surface with no fallback if it is wrong - under fork-and-build it IS the delivery mechanism. It must be validated end to end by someone who did not write it, from a clean GitHub account and a clean Apple Developer account, before the repository is announced.

The acknowledgments page's own facts foreclose any future project-published binary: the project does not own the OpenMinimed-derived copyright (GPL-3.0, relied on under palmarci / Pal Marci's explicit relicensing permission), and App Store terms conflict with GPL-3.0-only regardless. Worth surfacing in S1/S11 as a settled consequence, not a preference.

Three FRs in this section overlap owned surfaces in other sections and are deliberately scoped: FR-227 specifies the license viewer's behavior but 5.9 owns its Settings entry point; FR-219/FR-230 state docs and license gate conditions but 5.11 owns Required Check registration and workflow mechanics; FR-223 states what the install page must document but 5.10 owns the pipeline it describes.
parity_losses: Programmatic Bluetooth bond removal (BluetoothDevice.removeBond via reflection). iOS exposes no public or private API; bond removal is exclusively a user action in Settings > Bluetooth > (i) > Forget This Device. Three Tandem trust-recovery paths (status 0x05 before connect, status 0x08 with no prior session, 3 zero-response connections) and both Drivers' unpair paths become manual user procedures.

GATT service-cache invalidation on every connect (BluetoothGatt.refresh via reflection). iOS provides no way to flush a bonded peripheral's cached service database, so stale-cache silent notification loss is detected after the fact via the 3-zero-response-connections heuristic instead of pre-empted on every connect.

Link-layer disconnect status bytes (0x05 INSUFFICIENT_AUTHENTICATION, 0x08 INSUFFICIENT_ENCRYPTION, 0x13 CONN_TERMINATE_PEER_USER) are not exposed by Core Bluetooth. Failure classification becomes behavioural (rapid-disconnect timing, whether auth completed, whether any notification arrived) refined by a coarser system error vocabulary.

Manufacturer-specific advertisement data (company id 0x01F9, payload 0x00 || ASCII(localName) || 0x00). CBPeripheralManager accepts only local name and service UUIDs, so the Medtronic advertise-and-wait identity can only be carried as the standard GAP local name; the pump's matcher acceptance of that form is unproven.

Advertising interval, TX power, timeout and connectable-flag control. The ADVERTISE_MODE_LOW_LATENCY-for-reconnect vs ADVERTISE_MODE_BALANCED-for-first-pair distinction, which exists because a paired MiniMed pump scans infrequently, becomes unmitigable rather than tunable.

Background discoverability to a non-Apple central. A backgrounded iOS app has its advertised local name stripped and its service UUIDs relocated to an Apple-only overflow area, so advertise-and-wait pairing AND reconnection are foreground-only. Android's shipped promise that a paired Medtronic pump 'is remembered - GlycemicGPT reconnects on its own' is false on iOS.

Guaranteed background reconnection after user force-quit. iOS permanently suppresses Core Bluetooth relaunch for a force-quit app until the user manually reopens it; no entitlement, background mode or API changes this and there is no programmatic mitigation. START_STICKY and RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED have no equivalent for this case (reboot itself is covered by state restoration).

Foreground service and wake locks (PumpConnectionService, PARTIAL_WAKE_LOCK, 20 min timeout / 15 min renewal / 2 min reconnect lock). iOS has no equivalent execution construct, so Android's guaranteed 15 s background keep-alive poll cadence cannot be reproduced; background freshness is event-driven and best-effort.

Connection-parameter and MTU requests (requestConnectionPriority(CONNECTION_PRIORITY_HIGH) for a 7.5-15 ms interval, requestMtu(185)). Core Bluetooth gives the central no control over either; the app can only assert the negotiated write length after the fact.

A raw device address as a stable pairing key. Core Bluetooth never exposes a Bluetooth address; identity is an opaque per-installation UUID that is not stable across reinstall, device restore or an unbonded peripheral rotating its private address, requiring a name/serial fingerprint recovery path.

An undismissable, permanent out-of-app status surface. The Android foreground-service notification is permanent and always present; the iOS Lock Screen / Dynamic Island equivalent is user-dismissable and expires (roughly 8 h active, 12 h on the Lock Screen), so it cannot be the sole carrier of the Coverage Claim.

Re-prompting for Bluetooth permission. iOS never re-prompts after a denial, so Android's 'tap Scan again to re-request' recovery is unavailable; the only in-app recovery is a deep link into the app's Settings pane.

Runtime Driver installation is gone. Android lets a user sideload a DEX JAR into filesDir/plugins/ and run a community Driver with no repo change and no rebuild. iOS forbids executing code not signed into the bundle (App Store Review Guideline 2.5.2 plus OS-level code signing; TestFlight is not a carve-out). The Custom Plugins card, the Add Plugin document picker, the 50 MB / PK\x03\x04 ZIP-magic / canonical-path-containment install pipeline, and the 'Custom plugins are not verified by GlycemicGPT' trust warning are all deleted. Trying an unmerged Driver now requires forking, opening Xcode and signing with your own Apple credentials.

Runtime per-Driver containment is gone. Android's RestrictedContext throws SecurityException for ~30 Context operations and allowlists exactly seven system services (BLUETOOTH, LOCATION, POWER, ALARM, SENSOR, USB, WIFI), and ScopedCredentialProvider namespaces runtime-plugin credentials. iOS has no per-module runtime capability restriction: every compiled-in Driver shares one sandbox, one entitlement set, one container and one Keychain. Replaced by compile-time containment (build-graph dependency limits, CI import lint, CODEOWNERS review), which is stronger for what it covers but enforces nothing at runtime.

Registration is no longer guaranteed by compilation. Hilt's @Binds @IntoSet multibinding means an Android Driver that compiles is registered. Swift cannot enumerate protocol conformances at runtime, so a Driver that compiles but is missing from the Driver Catalog would be silently absent from the running app. Closed by a Required Check, but the failure mode itself is net-new to iOS.

Runtime Driver API-version rejection becomes a build-time assertion. Android rejects a version-mismatched Driver at load time (registry init and JAR load, exact equality); with compile-time linking that check is structurally unreachable. Not a functional loss to the user, but the enforcement moment moves from runtime to CI.

No guaranteed fixed-cadence refresh while the app is not in the foreground. Android's foreground service polled the Pump every 15 s (also the ~30 s BLE keep-alive); iOS offers only opportunistic BGAppRefreshTask and event-driven Core Bluetooth wakes, never a timer. Dashboard data can be arbitrarily old between foreground sessions; the app substitutes honest degradation (Stale at 6 min, Too Stale at 15 min, severity colour removed) plus an immediate re-read on every foreground activation.

Chart detail forced landscape: iOS has no 'sensor landscape' concept and no per-screen orientation property. The geometry request is honoured on iPhone but not on iPad, and it interacts with the user's rotation lock differently from Android's Activity.requestedOrientation. Restoration on every exit path is required to avoid a stuck orientation mask.

No system Bluetooth glyph on iOS. Android used Material's four Bluetooth icons for the six Pump-link states; iOS ships no equivalent SF Symbol and the Bluetooth SIG word/figure marks are trademark-encumbered. A custom glyph set must be shipped, and if the marks cannot be used the status-row glyph vocabulary diverges from the published Android status-icons documentation.

Do Not Disturb / Focus / silent-switch override: Android gets it free via ACCESS_NOTIFICATION_POLICY + setBypassDnd(true). iOS requires the Critical Alerts entitlement, granted per Team ID after manual Apple review — structurally unobtainable under fork-and-build. Urgent lows ship .timeSensitive; the ring/silent switch can silence them and the app cannot detect it.

Alarm volume boost and restore (AudioManager STREAM_ALARM to max on a low, persisted saved-volume, restored on acknowledge): deleted, not ported. iOS exposes no public API to set output or ringer volume, and none to read the silent-switch position or current ringer volume.

Custom per-notification vibration waveforms: Android's low channel [0, 500, 200, 500, 200, 500] has no iOS or watchOS analog. Severity is encoded in the sound plus a bounded temporal re-alarm ladder instead.

A permanently visible 'we are watching' indicator: Android's ongoing, non-dismissible pump foreground-service notification proves a process is alive and carries the coverage text. iOS has no ongoing notification, no foreground service, and no notification whose existence is evidence of a running process.

Backend-generated alert delivery to a suspended or terminated app: zero in v1 (APNs deferred). Android's foreground SSE service delivers continuously; on iOS the stream exists only while the process is alive.

Automatic restart of alerting after a device reboot: no launch-on-boot for third-party iOS apps under any entitlement. Nothing runs until the user unlocks the phone at least once, and a force-quit from the app switcher disables ALL background relaunch (including Core Bluetooth state restoration) until manual reopen.

Background Alert Floor evaluation cadence: Android evaluates on a 15-second foreground-service poll under a wake lock. iOS cadence is dictated entirely by Core Bluetooth wake events; the 360,000 ms Fresh window is the whole tolerance budget.
Per-severity custom notification sounds on the wrist: a notification mirrored onto Apple Watch plays watchOS's own default alert sound and haptic. The sound choice is an iPhone-only feature.

Android's setLocalOnly double-buzz avoidance has no iOS analog (iPhone notifications mirror to a worn Watch automatically with no per-notification opt-out); the compensating design is that system mirroring is the only wrist buzz path. Offsetting parity GAIN: the mirrored 'Got It' action carries the specific alert identifier and CAN silence an Alert Floor alarm, which the Android wrist dismiss provably cannot.

The draggable meal entry button — Android persists a per-device FAB position and exposes a 'Reset position to default' TalkBack action; iOS ships a fixed entry point above the tab bar plus a redundant Home list row, with drag dropped entirely.

In-process recovery from an oversized image decode — Android catches OutOfMemoryError and shows 'That photo is too large to process. Try a smaller one.'; iOS has no catchable out-of-memory condition (the system jetsams the process), so the same user-facing state is reachable only via a header-only pre-check plus a launch-time recovery marker after a termination.
Re-prompting for camera permission — Android can re-request after a first denial; iOS never re-prompts, so the app can only deep-link the user into the system Settings for the app.

Backgrounded chat request is lost: Android's process typically survives a backgrounded 90-second LLM call so a user can ask, switch apps and return to an answer; iOS suspends within seconds and the request dies. The app cancels on background and discloses it (FR-110). Not fixable without introducing chat persistence, which would create a durable store of health-related conversation content that Android deliberately does not have.

Chat entry point on the wrist is user-placed and may be absent entirely: Android ships its own watch face with a guaranteed AI Chat complication slot; watchOS permits no third-party faces, so chat is reachable only from a WidgetKit accessory complication and a Smart Stack widget the user must add manually.
Chat glyph colour is not guaranteed: Android tints the chat complication blue (0xFF3B82F6); watchOS accessory rendering applies the face's tint, so the glyph must be identifiable in monochrome.
'Online' voice indicator dropped: Android labels TTS voices that require a network connection; iOS exposes no equivalent flag on AVSpeechSynthesisVoice, so the label is removed rather than guessed.

Persisted TTS voice identifiers do not migrate: an Android ai_tts_voice value never resolves on iOS. No cross-platform settings migration path exists or should be built; the unknown-voice fallback to the system voice covers it.

Watch dictation is not testable in the developer loop: watchOS dictation does not function in the Simulator and the lead developer has no Apple Watch, so the primary Watch chat input path can only be validated by the maintainer on hardware.

No custom watch faces: the Android `:watchface` module (DIGITAL_FULL and ANALOG_MECHANICAL, WFF v2, 450x450 circular, five-slot and three-slot layouts with DefaultProviderPolicy binding our own providers, branding text, per-variant overlay defaults) has no watchOS equivalent. The user places complications themselves and the app cannot guarantee glucose, IOB, graph and coverage are visible together on one face.

No Watch Face Push and no phone-set active face: neither the transport (WatchFacePusher / WatchFaceInstaller / DWF validation token / SET_PUSHED_WATCH_FACE_AS_ACTIVE) nor the concept exists on watchOS, and pushing an executable artifact to a paired device is separately prohibited by App Review Guideline 2.5.2.
No phone-controlled watch face theme (dark / clinical_blue / high_contrast) and no phone-controlled seconds display: Apple owns face colour and time rendering. (Both were already inert on Android.)

No custom background haptic waveform on the wrist: the Android urgent double-buzz (0/500/200/500 ms) versus one-shot 300 ms distinction cannot be reproduced, because watchOS has no API to vibrate from the background without a notification. Urgency is carried by interruption level and sound instead, and per binding decision 4 the wrist alarm can be silenced by the ring/silent switch with the app unable to detect it.

Complication colour is not ours: watchOS renders complications in an accented/tinted mode, so the Android alerts bell's six-branch hue encoding (grey / amber / red) and the sparkline's four colour-encoded overlay layers (basal teal/blue-grey, bolus pink/orange/purple, IOB blue, activity-mode purple/orange) do not survive. The multi-overlay full-colour graph exists only inside the Watch app and on iPhone widgets.

No guaranteed periodic heartbeat: Android's 3-minute coverage heartbeat (max(timeout/2, 5 s) from a foreground service) cannot be reproduced on iOS. Replaced by an absolute expiry piggybacked on Core Bluetooth-driven writes. A force-quit app is never relaunched by Core Bluetooth, and the wrist's decay to 'no recent data' is the only signal the user gets.

Metered wrist refresh: high-priority wrist complication transfers draw on an OS daily allowance (Android has no cap). Freshness and coverage decay are free via pre-baked timelines, but a data-driven wrist refresh is not guaranteed per Glucose Reading.

No watch-side self-update and no separate watch artifact: the Android WearAppUpdateChecker / WearApkPusher / PackageInstaller path and the documented ADB sideload route are removed entirely. Net improvement (the Watch app ships in the bundle), but the capability 'update the watch app from the phone' no longer exists.

No guaranteed periodic background execution: Android's retention worker (guaranteed daily) and Nightscout periodic sync (guaranteed 15-minute floor) become opportunistic on iOS and may not run for days on a rarely opened app.

The outbound queue does not drain continuously in the background. Android's foreground service drained every 3 seconds forever; iOS drains only in the foreground and in system-granted windows, so upload latency is materially worse and has no upper bound.

After an iPhone restart or a force-quit, no data is captured, no upload occurs and no alerting happens until the user opens the app. Android's BootCompletedReceiver has no substitute and no code can run to detect the condition while it holds.
Server-generated alerts do not reach a suspended or terminated app: the event stream is foreground-only and background pulls are opportunistic (consequence of the settled APNs-deferred decision).
Deferred uploads may be marked discretionary by the system and held for an unbounded time; the app cannot force delivery, whereas Android's queue drained on its own schedule.
Local Network access is an additional permission gate with no Android analog: a denial breaks a LAN-hosted Backend and presents as a dead server unless the app explicitly names it.

Alert sounds: no system ringtone picker, no arbitrary content URI, no persistable read permission — iOS exposes no API to enumerate, preview or select the system sound library; only bundled files (<=30s, PCM/MA4/uLaw/aLaw as .aiff/.wav/.caf) can be a notification sound.

No notification channel model: iOS has no per-category OS notification settings, so a user who mutes the app in iOS Settings mutes low alerts, high alerts and AI notifications together — Android lets each be tuned independently.

'Boost Volume for Lows' cannot exist: no iOS API raises system output volume, and nothing overrides the ring/silent switch for ordinary notifications. Loudness over silent requires Critical Alerts, structurally unobtainable under fork-and-build (decision 4).

No watch-face gallery, no face push, no face-level configuration (e.g. Show Seconds): watchOS supports no third-party watch faces. The Digital Full and Analog Mechanical designs with their basal/bolus/IOB/activity-mode graph overlays are lost; complications and Smart Stack widgets are non-equivalent substitutes.

No in-app self-update: the check -> download -> size-verify -> install state machine is impossible on iOS. Only version detection plus an 'Open TestFlight' action remains, and the Builder owns the 90-day TestFlight rebuild.
No watch-app push: the Watch App Update card's download -> push -> install machine, its 100 MB cap and its 15s install timer have no iOS counterpart; the Watch app ships inside the phone app bundle.

No runtime/custom Driver install: the Custom Plugins card, Add Plugin from a user-supplied archive, per-Driver Remove that deletes its settings, and the untrusted-source warning all disappear (decision 1). Verification Status replaces the install-time trust warning.

No battery-optimization exemption: Android's isIgnoringBatteryOptimizations card and its Settings intent have no iOS equivalent. Substituted by a Reliability card reporting background-refresh status, Low Power Mode, and force-quit (which stops Core Bluetooth state restoration).

App Transport Security cannot be scoped to private/LAN IP ranges: exceptions are per-domain and accept neither IPs nor CIDR, and NSAllowsLocalNetworking covers only .local and link-local, not RFC1918. The app's own private-address-only policy becomes the sole guard against cleartext to a public host, a security property Android gets platform help with.

iOS 14+ Local Network Privacy adds a failure mode Android has no counterpart for: a LAN Backend is unreachable until the user grants permission, the prompt appears once, denial is permanent until they visit iOS Settings, and it cannot be re-prompted in-app. The Simulator neither presents nor enforces it.

No project-published installable binary and no in-app self-update: the entire AppUpdateChecker / WearAppUpdateChecker / dev-latest install channel and the APK download hardening around it have no iOS target (no sideload path, no package installer, guideline 2.5.2 forbids downloading and executing code). Replaced by TestFlight plus a read-only upstream release notice.

An installed build expires 90 days after upload and stops launching; an Android APK runs indefinitely. For a glucose monitor this is a silent loss of monitoring, mitigated but not eliminated by scheduled rebuild and in-app expiry surfacing.

GitHub disables scheduled workflows after 60 days of repository inactivity — 30 days BEFORE the TestFlight build expires — so a quiet fork can lose its automatic rebuild while the Builder believes it is armed. No Android analogue.

The fixed release-signer fingerprint equality check (RELEASE_SIGNER_SHA256=55f0d0cd…) cannot exist, because every Builder signs with their own Apple Distribution certificate. Replaced by a property assertion (Apple Distribution identity, get-task-allow == false, TeamIdentifier match, unexpired profile); nothing structurally ties a build to a project-known identity.
No Gradle-wrapper-checksum equivalent for the Xcode toolchain. Toolchain trust reduces to the GitHub-hosted runner image plus an in-repo version pin.

Every Builder must hold and annually renew a paid Apple Developer Program membership, and their distribution certificate and provisioning profile expire on a one-year cycle. Android required no account, no renewal, and no per-user cost. A free Apple account cannot use TestFlight at all (7-day sideload profiles instead).

Per-Builder App ID registration is mandatory because Apple's App ID namespace is globally unique across all developer accounts; an Android applicationId is just a string. Largest new setup burden, with no Android counterpart.

Side-by-side stable and development installs are not free: Android got them from applicationIdSuffix ".debug"; iOS needs a second App ID, profile and App Store Connect record per Builder. Not provided in v1.

Watch-face build artifacts disappear entirely — no GlycemicGPT-WatchFace-Digital/Analog APKs to produce, sign, publish, or carve out of the certificate assertion. Better on the signing axis (Android's watch-face APKs were debug-signed) but a lost capability.

The upstream project cannot verify what any installed build contains. Because every Builder compiles and signs their own binary, every published architectural claim is a claim about source at a stated tag, not about the binary anyone is running.

macOS runner minutes carry roughly a 10x multiplier on private repositories, so a Builder who makes their fork private can exhaust the free allowance in a handful of iOS-plus-watchOS builds and lose the ability to rebuild before expiry. Android's Linux-runner builds had no such pressure.

SAST depth: Semgrep p/kotlin + p/java have no Swift equivalent of comparable breadth from any vendor. CodeQL swift + security-extended, Semgrep p/secrets, gitleaks and project-specific SwiftLint custom rules are the honest replacement, but a green Static Analysis Gate on iOS carries measurably less assurance than the same-shaped gate on Android. Naming-only port of the Semgrep packs would yield a permanently green check that tests nothing.

Manifest and network-security linting: Android Lint is the named verifier for HTTPS enforcement and the compensating control cited in Android's MobSF decline. Apple ships nothing comparable (xcodebuild analyze covers C/Objective-C, not Swift, and never inspects Info.plist or entitlements). The Entitlements and Plist Guard covers the specific posture class deterministically but is narrower.

Artifact-level scanning is unreachable upstream: under fork-and-build the project holds no signing identity, so upstream CI cannot produce a signed device build and the iOS analogue of APK-artifact SAST cannot exist upstream even in principle. Android's accepted residual gap (secrets present only in the built artifact) persists and widens slightly.

Upstream cannot gate the binary each user installs: on Android upstream CI built the APK users side-loaded, so every gate ran against the exact artifact. Here the installed binary is produced by the Builder's own workflow run, from their fork, at their chosen commit, signed with their certificate. Upstream can require no status check there.

Dependency CVE coverage: SwiftPM advisories in OSV and the GitHub Advisory Database are materially sparser than Maven's (Android's baseline was ~1,175 resolved packages clean), and remote SPM binaryTarget dependencies have no resolvable package identity so they cannot be CVE-scanned at all. Gradle lockfiles had no such hole.

Simulator-level BLE smoke coverage: Core Bluetooth does not exist in the iOS Simulator (CBCentralManager never reaches poweredOn), whereas the Android emulator at least presented a non-functional Bluetooth stack. Neither CI ever tested BLE against real hardware, so release-gate parity is preserved; what is lost is Simulator-level smoke, replaced by trace-replay tests over recorded frames and the Simulated Driver.

No project-published binary and no 'download the topmost release' path; the install runbook gates on paid Apple Developer Program membership before any use - a hard access barrier Android did not have.

TestFlight builds expire after 90 days. A Builder who stops rebuilding loses a working glucose monitor; a sideloaded APK simply kept running. An expired build does not launch, so it does not monitor and does not alert.
No in-app 'Check for updates' that downloads and installs. The update mechanism is TestFlight plus re-running the fork's workflow; the app can at most compare tags and show a non-actionable banner.

No custom watch face. The watch setup page documents complications the user places manually on an Apple-provided face, with no control of the face surface, no guarantee of placement, and no guaranteed refresh cadence.

The published alert-delivery warning is strictly longer and more pessimistic than Android's: a .timeSensitive urgent-low alert can be silenced by the ring/silent switch and the app cannot detect it, and server-generated alerts do not reach a suspended or terminated app in v1 (APNs deferred), degrading caregiver alerting.
The battery-optimization exemption documented as a prerequisite on two Android pages has no iOS counterpart, and the '<5%/day' battery figure is deliberately dropped rather than inherited.

The device verification table starts almost empty: only Tandem t:slim X2 can reach Verified in v1, and only after DanielDanielson validates on their own hardware from their own fork. No Android device status may be inherited.
The runtime-loaded plugin contribution path is deleted from the contributor guide rather than adapted; adding a Pump requires a source change, a merged PR, and a rebuild by each Builder.

iOS pages cannot reuse Android page basenames (mobile/install.md, troubleshooting/cant-pair-pump.md, daily-use/connecting-medtronic-pump.md all collide), so existing cross-repository links in the Android tree do not resolve to iOS pages and must be re-pointed deliberately.
open_questions: Spike (b): whether a 780G's discovery filter accepts an iOS advertisement carrying the identity as a standard GAP local name rather than as manufacturer-specific data under company id 0x01F9. Needs a physical pump; neither the lead developer nor DanielDanielson has one. Who validates, and does FR-6 ship gated behind an unvalidated label until they do?

Whether an already-bonded Medtronic pump will reconnect to a backgrounded iPhone by stored peer identity rather than by advertised name. If it does, FR-16's foreground-only degradation is narrower than stated. Cannot be assumed and cannot be tested without hardware.
The 2-minute scan auto-stop and the 10 s discovered-device age-out have no Android counterpart. Confirm both values or accept them as newly introduced for iOS.
Should the 45 s connect watchdog be user-visible as a countdown, or silent until it fires?
Android's live CGM path and live basal path have known validation gaps that the pairing/connection layer does not touch; flagged only so 5.3 does not assume 5.1 resolved them.
Does the iOS Driver API version constant reset to 1 for the new SDK, or inherit Android's 5 to keep cross-repo changelogs aligned?

Should the Simulated Driver and Trace-Replay Driver be excludable from a release build via the build-time kill switch, or always present? Excluding them removes their coverage from the artifact that actually ships; including them puts two non-clinical data sources in the Driver list a Builder could activate by mistake.

Data sync has no Capability protocol on Android - it is a pure activation and mutual-exclusion tag. Keep it that way, or give it a protocol now that a Backend-mediated Nightscout source is a first-class shipped source?

Verification Status is net-new metadata with no Android equivalent. Who assigns it, and does a change to a Driver's protocol code automatically demote it from Verified pending re-validation on DanielDanielson's hardware?
Trace-Replay fixtures: what is the de-identification standard, and who reviews a submitted trace before it lands in a public repo?

CGM-active percentage assumes exactly 12 Glucose Readings per hour (Android behaviour). A source with a different cadence misreports coverage - should the expected cadence be declared by the Driver's glucose-source Capability instead of hard-coded?

SI-5 forbids the Alert Floor from firing on thresholds neither the user nor their Backend set, but FR-47's severity banding colours from the default Alert Threshold set (55/70/180/250) when nothing has been set. Confirm colouring from defaults is acceptable while alerting from them is not, and that the two are visibly distinguishable.

Dynamic Type and the fixed 64pt hero numeral: Android has no equivalent, so there is no reference behaviour. Does the hero value scale with Dynamic Type at all, or stay fixed while only surrounding text scales?
Is iPad a supported target for this release? FR-56 (chart detail landscape) assumes iPhone only.

Carried from research and unanswerable from the Android repo: when the iPhone is suspended or unreachable, what must the Watch app still be able to show? (Owned by 5.7, but it constrains what the dashboard's data relay must produce.)

Coverage Claim wording without Critical Alerts: 'watching' vs 'watching, but you may not hear it'. Strict SI-6 argues for the caveat; it would show for nearly every Builder nearly always, risking desensitization of the one surface built to be believed.
FR-76 re-alarm ladder cadence and cap (currently 5 repeats at 120 s) is invented, not ported — needs real-user tuning before the first tagged release.

Achievable background Core Bluetooth evaluation cadence against a real t:slim X2 is unmeasured and gates whether the 360,000 ms Fresh window is honest. Requires DanielDanielson's fork build on their own hardware.

Whether the informational tier (iob_warning, no_data, unknown types) should be permitted to break through Focus at all, given Android routes it to a non-DND-bypassing channel and iOS .active is the honest equivalent — confirmed as-is but worth a ruling if caregivers complain about missed data-gap alerts.
Does the Backend return an image for a food record, or does the Home recent-meal card keep Android's neutral placeholder thumbnail permanently?
Is the read-only re-log sheet acceptable for v1, or should the port block on the Backend gaining a create-record-from-common-food path?
Should the 5xx meal diagnostic log survive at all under SI-9, given the error body can contain food identity and carb values?
Is the SI-12 carve-out for the two dispersion flags approved, and should the Contract Pin mark them optional-with-default?
Is the BG-at-event unit conversion (a deliberate divergence from Android's raw mg/dL column) approved as an intentional Parity Ledger entry?
Is a debug-only bundled-sample-photo injector in v1 scope, given the Simulator has no camera and the capture path is otherwise unreachable in the developer's loop?
Confirm the Backend's actual AI inference ceiling so the single AI request timeout is set from evidence rather than inherited from Android's 90 s.

Confirm that GET /api/ai/provider returning exactly 404 for 'no provider configured' is pinned by the Contract Pin, since it is the sole discriminator between the terminal no-provider state and the retryable offline state.
Should the 'Disable TTS' menu copy be renamed to match the 'spoken responses' vocabulary used elsewhere in this section, accepting a deliberate copy divergence from Android?
Does the maintainer's device pass for watchOS dictation need to gate release, given the lead developer has no Apple Watch and dictation does not function in the watchOS Simulator?

Should the Watch app hold a Backend credential and fetch independently in Backend-connected mode, or does every wrist value come from the app only? (Affects FR-122, FR-126 and the Keychain threat model; 5.8 owns the answer.)
Is a shareable watch-face configuration file in scope for v1 as the closest analogue to Android's watch-face variant push, given it is device-only and unverifiable in the Simulator? (FR-118)
Confirm the unified graph Y clamp is 20/500 and not 40/400. (FR-133)
Confirm the live glanceable surface's OS lifetime bound against the shipping iOS/watchOS version, and confirm the restart policy when it expires overnight. (FR-119)
Does the project accept rebinding the Android 'theme' control to a Watch-app-only high-contrast appearance preference, or should the control be deleted outright? (FR-134)
What is the real per-Driver enqueue rate? The 20,000-row queue bound is sized from Tandem's 15-second fast cadence; a Driver with a different cadence changes the day-without-upload arithmetic.
Should the alert history follow the user's chosen retention window (1-30 days) or stay pinned at Android's fixed 7 days? The former is more predictable; the latter is exact parity.

Under fork-and-build, does the project ship the release Info.plist with local-networking permitted and arbitrary loads only in a debug configuration, and is a Builder who edits those values still inside the supported build surface (5.10)?

Should the Settings Network section carry its own persistent 'Local Network access denied' banner alongside the insecure-transport banner, or is the in-section card of FR-162 sufficient? The condition is invisible in the Simulator and will otherwise be misdiagnosed as a server fault.

FR-176 gates the Developer section on a debug build, but under fork-and-build a Builder can build the debug configuration and install it through their own TestFlight — putting fault injection (simulate-backend-unreachable, fast-staleness, CGM injection) on a real user's phone. Confirm whether that is acceptable or whether the gate must additionally require a non-TestFlight install.

Does the ATS posture need explicit App Review justification text drafted, given internal TestFlight distribution under a Builder's own account triggers no Beta App Review (per the critic's resolution) but a Builder who later distributes externally would?

Which bundled alert sounds ship, and who authors/licenses them? FR-170 requires an alarm-like low set distinct from the notification-like high/AI set, but the sound assets themselves are unspecified and must be GPL-3.0-compatible.
Must a Builder be able to run the stable build and the development build on the same iPhone at the same time? Determines whether FR-182 registers one App ID set or two per Builder.
Does the lead keep a 1Password-backed local signing convenience path for their own maintainer/validation builds, or is every signing path fork-owned with no exception?
What is the committed scheduled-rebuild cadence and the exact escalation thresholds for the in-app expiry countdown (30/14/7/3/1 days assumed)?
Is a 90-day retention on upstream Simulator .app release assets sufficient, given that upstream release assets are the only artifact the lead can run?

Does the upstream repository commit to remaining public indefinitely? macOS runner minutes carry a ~10x multiplier on private repositories, and a private upstream would put the required-check set under cost pressure.

Should CodeRabbit's fail_commit_status be flipped to true so its mode: error Medical Safety and BLE Protocol Safety checks actually block merge, or does it stay advisory now that those invariants are enforced mechanically?
What is the promotion criterion that moves UI Tests (Simulator) from non-required to a sixth Required Check?
What licenses go on the dependency license allowlist at day one, and who arbitrates a request to add one (project lead alone, or lead plus a licensing review)?

Should the required-check roster comparison step read the branch-protection ruleset via the API (needs a token with admin read) or compare against a committed copy of the ruleset? The first is authoritative but not fork-runnable; the second is fork-safe but can itself drift.

Does the project want gitleaks as a hard-failing step inside Static Analysis Gate (as specified in FR-200), given Android deliberately declined a third secret-scanning pass on the grounds that Semgrep p/secrets plus CodeRabbit gitleaks plus org-wide GitGuardian already covered it? The iOS change is justified by CodeRabbit's non-blocking commit status, but it is a divergence from a recorded Android decision.

Counsel review of the manufacturer framing: Android reserves 'users become the manufacturer of their own personal medical device' (Loop/AndroidAPS precedent) for third-party forks that add device control, but under fork-and-build that description arguably fits EVERY user. Does the iOS disclaimer need counsel review before the install runbook is published, and if the framing applies, does that change whether fork-and-build instructions are published publicly or only how the disclaimer is worded? This gates the two highest-traffic published pages.
What is the single canonical deployment floor to publish - iOS 17 / watchOS 10 or iOS 18 / watchOS 11? The evidence carries both; every page must quote the same number.
Does the website repository accept a platform-scoped section set (docs/ios/, docs/apple-watch/) without changes here, and who owns adding the merged-tree link check to that repository?

Should the fork template ship a scheduled workflow that rebuilds automatically before the 90-day expiry, or is an automatic rebuild a Builder never sees a worse failure mode than a build that visibly lapses?

Is a Builder who edits the disclaimer, adds a Sentry DSN, or changes an Alert Threshold default in their own fork still described as running 'GlycemicGPT' in these documents, and does the privacy document need to say so explicitly?
